plotStats.title: Diversity statistics
plotStats.chaoNeedsData: Chao estimates unavailable: Chao1 needs individual counts; Chao2 needs ≥2 subplots.
plotStats.chaoNone: Chao estimates unavailable (no usable incidence data in subplots yet).
plotStats.lossyNote: Mixed units present — indices are indicative only.
plotStats.lowerBoundNote: Chao estimators are lower bounds of true richness.

basis.mixed: Mixed abundance units, weighted after numericisation.

plotStats.crossHint: Estimates the species pool of the area these plots sample, with each plot as one incidence unit. Select only plots from the same area, vegetation type and protocol — mixing different species pools computes, but means nothing.
plotStats.crossNeedTwo: Select at least 2 plots to compute Chao2.
plotStats.crossEmpty: The selected plots have no species records yet.
plotStats.selectedPlots: Using the {{n}} selected plots as sampling units
plotStats.betaNeedTwo: Select exactly 2 plots to compare β similarity (Sørensen/Jaccard).
plotStats.dominantNote: Percentages are relative values under the current basis (relative cover / density / basal area).
plotStats.dominantNoteFreq: Percentages are relative values; frequency = subplots occupied ÷ subplots sampled. A full IVI (relative frequency + density + dominance) needs density and basal area recorded together — only the derivable components are shown.

report.notAvailable: Record not found — no report to show.
report.conservationNote: Counts are per species; redlist and IUCN exclude non-threatened categories (LC/NLC/NE/NA).
report.coverOver100: Ground cover sums to {{total}}%, above 100% — please check the entries.
report.trackTooShort: Track too short; species per km not computed.
report.methodsShannon: Shannon–Wiener index H′ = −Σ pᵢ ln pᵢ, where pᵢ is the relative abundance of species i; exp(H′) is the effective number of species.
report.methodsSimpson: Simpson concentration D = Σ pᵢ²; this report gives 1−D and the inverse 1/D.
report.methodsEvenness: Pielou evenness J′ = H′ / ln S, where S is richness; undefined for S < 2.
report.methodsDominance: Berger–Parker dominance d = max(pᵢ), the share of the most abundant species; its inverse 1/d is the effective number of dominants.
report.methodsChao: Chao1 estimates richness from abundance data (f1, f2 = species represented by exactly 1 and 2 individuals); Chao2 from incidence data (q1, q2 = species found in exactly 1 and 2 sampling units). Both are lower bounds of true richness.
report.methodsCoverage: Sample coverage C = 1 − f1/n (Good–Turing), n = total individuals; completeness is observed richness divided by the estimate.
report.methodsProvenance: Formulas follow: vegan package documentation, Chao (1984, 1987), Chao et al. (2014, Ecological Monographs 84:45–67), Curtis & McIntosh (1951).
report.chartEffort: Observed vs estimated richness per plot
report.crossChao2Note: Estimates the species pool of the area sampled, with each plot as one incidence unit; confirm the plots share an area, vegetation type and protocol.
report.similarityNote: Sørensen = 2C/(A+B), presence-based and independent of abundance.
report.formatHtml: HTML (opens in a browser, prints to PDF)
report.effortMixedEstimators: Plots qualify for different estimators (Chao1 needs individual counts, Chao2 needs ≥2 subplots), which cannot be compared in one chart, so no estimate is shown.
report.plotsMixedBasis: Plots use different abundance bases; the indices are not directly comparable across rows.
report.maxAbundanceMixed: Abundance units are mixed across the project, so this column has no common unit and indicates relative magnitude only.
report.dbhClassNote: Class width {{width}} cm; diameters {{min}}–{{max}} cm; quadratic mean diameter {{qmd}} cm.
report.iviComponents: IV is the mean of {{n}} relative values ({{list}}), scaled 0–100 and summing to 100 across species, per the specification\u2019s IV = (rel. density + rel. dominance + rel. frequency) x 100/3.

areaSource.subplots: Area is the sum of the subplot rectangles.
areaSource.sample-size: Area converted from the recorded plot size.

areaUnknown.no-sample-size: No plot size recorded, so per-hectare figures cannot be computed.
areaUnknown.unrecognised-unit: The plot-size unit "{{unit}}" is not a recognised area unit, so no per-hectare figure is given rather than one that could be wrong by orders of magnitude.
areaUnknown.non-positive: The recorded plot size is not positive, so per-hectare figures cannot be computed.
areaUnknown.subplot-dims-missing: Some subplots lack a width or length; summing them would under-report the area and inflate every density, so no per-hectare figure is given.
areaUnknown.zero-radius: No point-count radius recorded, so the area is unknown.

iviDominance.cover: Dominance is relative cover, not basal area.

report.diversityIndexSource: Indices follow the diversity section of the Taiwan plant-ecology assessment specification (Ludwig & Reynolds, 1988).
report.pooledNote: The All row is recomputed over every record pooled, not averaged across the rows above, so it can exceed any single plot.
report.dualBasisNote: Woody data is computed on both bases: basal area is the app\u2019s own weighting (a single large tree genuinely dominates a stand), while stem counts follow the Taiwan assessment specification\u2019s rule that woody plants are counted by stems. They answer different questions, so both are shown rather than one being chosen.
report.groupSplitNote: This section covers {{group}} only. Diversity indices, importance values and richness estimates are not comparable across taxonomic groups — the survey method, the counting unit and the species pool all differ — so they are computed separately per higher taxon.
report.sortHint: Tap to sort by this column
report.conservationSpeciesNote: Every species carrying a Red List, IUCN, CITES, protected or endemic status, ordered by the highest threat category it holds (EX > EW > RE > CR > EN > VU > NT > DD). "–" means unlisted or a non-threatened category.
report.expandHint: Tap to show the full text
report.rarefactionNote: The band is a 95% confidence interval from the unconditional bootstrap of Chao et al. (2014) Appendix G ({{b}} replicates).
report.extrapolationBound: Extrapolation stops at double the reference sample, which the source marks "reliable if m* < n".
report.rarefactionSource: Interpolation uses the minimum-variance unbiased estimator (Chao et al. 2014, Ecological Monographs 84:45–67, Tables 1 and 2); coverage follows Chao & Jost (2012).

rarefactionUnavailable.not-counts: A rarefaction curve needs individual counts or several sampling units; cover values have no individuals to rarefy, so no curve is drawn.
rarefactionUnavailable.need-2-units: A rarefaction curve needs at least 2 sampling units (subplots, or plots).

dq.noAbundance: {{records}} records carry no quantity (affecting {{species}} species recorded as presence only); diversity indices use only the quantified ones.
dq.genusOnly: {{n}} taxa are identified to genus only (e.g. {{examples}}); such records inflate the species count.
dq.aboveGenus: {{n}} taxa are identified above genus (e.g. {{examples}}) and should not count towards richness.
dq.rankUnknown: {{n}} taxa have no rank information, so species level cannot be confirmed.
dq.mixedUnits: Abundance units are mixed ({{kinds}}); values in different units cannot be added, so the indices are indicative only.
dq.unparseable: {{n}} quantities could not be read as numbers (e.g. {{examples}}).
dq.singletons: {{n}} species were recorded as a single individual (singletons); the Chao estimates rest largely on these.
dq.doubletons: {{n}} species were recorded as exactly two individuals (doubletons).
dq.noSubplot: {{n}} records have no subplot; incidence-based figures skip them.
dq.clean: No data issues affecting the statistics above were detected.
dq.note: This section states facts, not faults — identifying to genus is ordinary field practice, but it affects the species count, so it is reported.

report.methodsSpecIndices: Diversity indices follow the set listed in the Taiwan plant-ecology assessment specification: S, λ, H′, N₁ = e^H′, N₂ = 1/λ and E5 = [(1/λ)−1]/[e^H′−1] (Ludwig & Reynolds, 1988). Woody data is reported on both a basal-area and a stem-count basis.
report.methodsStand: Stems and basal area per hectare are scaled by the plot area; basal area is Σπ(d/2)² over the recorded stem diameters. The area source (summed subplot rectangles, πr² for a point count, or the recorded plot size) is stated in that section; an unrecognised unit yields no per-hectare figure and a stated reason.
report.methodsDbhClasses: Diameter classes are 5 cm wide, the first beginning at the 1 cm recording threshold the specification sets for woody stems; the width doubles when the class count would exceed the limit, keeping the edges on round numbers.
report.methodsIvi: Importance value IV = (relative density + relative dominance + relative frequency) × 100/3 (Curtis & McIntosh, 1951; Taiwan assessment specification). Relative frequency is a species\u2019 frequency divided by the summed frequencies of all species. Where a component is unavailable the mean of the available components is used, keeping the 0–100 scale, and the component count is stated with the table.
report.methodsRarefaction: Rarefaction uses the minimum-variance unbiased interpolation estimators of Chao et al. (2014), Tables 1 and 2, with extrapolation stopping at double the reference sample. The 95% band is the unconditional bootstrap of their Appendix G (200 replicates), seeded from the data so the interval is reproducible. Sample coverage follows Chao & Jost (2012).
report.methodsDataQuality: The data-quality section reports unquantified records, identification rank, mixed units and the number of rare species, so the applicability of the statistics above can be judged.
report.rankAbundanceNote: The value axis is logarithmic. A steep line means a few species dominate; a long shallow tail means an even community. No single index shows this shape.
report.rankAbundanceDropped: {{n}} species carry no positive abundance and are not on the curve.
report.rankAbundanceMixed: Abundance units are mixed; values in different units cannot be ranked against one another, so no rank–abundance curve is drawn.
report.profileMissingHeight: {{n}} strata have no height and cannot be placed on the axis; they remain in the table.
report.profileDegraded: The Word version spaces the strata evenly — DrawingML cannot encode both a band\u2019s position and its cover — so see the HTML version or the app for the metric profile.
report.profileNoHeights: No stratum has a height, so cover bars are shown instead of a profile.
